en.quick:
“HVDC system” in power-system exams normally refers to a high-voltage DC transmission link embedded between AC systems. The conversion terminals are what allow two AC systems—including asynchronous systems—to exchange power over a DC link. Key relation: Typical chain: AC generation/grid → AC/DC converter → HVDC line/cable → DC/AC converter → AC transmission/distribution grid.

Exam focus: HVDC changes the transmission medium, not the conventional AC nature of generation and distribution grids. Common trap: Reading “HVDC” as if the entire power system from generator to consumer were DC.
formula: Typical chain: AC generation/grid → AC/DC converter → HVDC line/cable → DC/AC converter → AC transmission/distribution grid.

hi.quick: D — दोनों AC। HVDC केवल पारेषण माध्यम बदलता है: AC उत्पादन → रेक्टिफायर → HVDC लाइन → इन्वर्टर → AC पारेषण/वितरण ग्रिड। उत्पादन और वितरण पारंपरिक रूप से AC ही रहते हैं।
